matrix.question: general reuse
matrix.evidence: Eurostat notice: "Reuse of statistical data, metadata, publications, and other dissemination tools published on this website for commercial or non-commercial purposes is authorised provided the source is acknowledged"; implemented by Commission Decision 2011/833/EU (documents available for reuse without charge, without individual application, subject only to acknowledgement / no distortion / non-liability).

matrix.question: commercial reuse
matrix.evidence: same sentence names commercial purposes explicitly; notice: "How to re-use Eurostat material for commercial purposes: there is no special procedure or requirement for a written licence"; ESS policy: statistics free "irrespective of subsequent commercial or non-commercial use". Not inferred from public accessibility.
matrix.requirement: only the conditions below; the commercial-use exclusions do not cover this dataset (see Türkiye / third-party rows)

matrix.question: automated API access
matrix.evidence: Eurostat publishes SDMX 2.1 web services for programmatic access to its datasets (web-services page); no registration, key or contractual term found; robots.txt does not disallow /eurostat/api/.
matrix.requirement: use the documented API; honour HTTP 429/5xx

matrix.question: systematic retrieval
matrix.status: YES (no prohibition found; no published quota)
matrix.evidence: Reuse is authorised without restriction other than acknowledgement; the official page documents a fixed update schedule (twice daily, 11:00 and 23:00 CET) and that only the latest version is kept; no rate limit, fair-use clause or ban on periodic retrieval was found in the notice, the Decision, the web-services page or robots.txt. "API exists" was NOT treated as sufficient: permission rests on the reuse authorisation + the absence of any contrary term.
matrix.requirement: polite use: ≤ 1 request/second, daily cadence, bounded unit, stop on 429; no published quota exists (UNKNOWN, treated conservatively)

matrix.question: attribution
matrix.evidence: notice "How to cite": datasets "Source: [DOI], [access date]"; customised versions "Source: [Eurostat dataset datacode link], [access date]"; Decision art. 6(2)(a).
matrix.requirement: store and display the canonical attribution below

matrix.question: modification notice
matrix.evidence: notice: "When reuse involves … modifications to the data or text, this must be stated clearly to the end user… A disclaimer regarding the non-responsibility of Eurostat shall be included." Decision art. 6(2)(b)-(c): do not distort the original meaning; non-liability.
matrix.requirement: values are stored as published (no recalculation); selection/restructuring/derived products must say so and carry the non-responsibility disclaimer; never present a derived figure as Eurostat's

matrix.question: third-party rights
matrix.evidence: notice: all data on the Eurostat website is regarded as Eurostat's unless explicitly stated otherwise; the response annotations name SOURCE_INSTITUTIONS = Eurostat; the ESMS says data are collected by Eurostat from national statistical institutes and carries no third-party/copyright restriction text. This is absence of evidence of a restriction, not proof none exists.
matrix.requirement: stop and re-review if a response or metadata ever carries a third-party/copyright notice

matrix.question: Türkiye data
matrix.evidence: The notice's non-commercial-only exception covers "Data for countries other than: Member States of the EU, Member States of EFTA, official EU acceding and candidate countries". Türkiye has been an official EU candidate country since the December 1999 Helsinki European Council (enlargement.ec.europa.eu, retrieved 2026-10-05) and the demo_mor ESMS lists "EU candidate countries" in its reference area. The old exception text was re-read from the current notice, not carried forward.
matrix.requirement: keep the reader's geography catalog inside EU/EFTA/candidate countries and EU aggregates (TR, DE, EU27_2020). "Other countries" (e.g. US, JP, CN, UK, Russia, Armenia…) are NON-COMMERCIAL ONLY: never add them without a new review

matrix.question: DEMO_MLEXPEC-specific restriction
matrix.evidence: the dataset response carries 14 annotation types and none is a licence/restriction; its ESMS (demo_mor) contains no licence, reuse, restriction or third-party text; the general notice says individual notices may narrow the terms and none was found.

proposals.PROPOSED_PRODUCTION_D1_BUDGET: 40 D1 calls and 160 statements per invocation (expected 36 / 145)
proposals.PROPOSED_D1_HARD_STOP: 44 D1 calls per invocation: abort BEFORE issuing the next call (the checkpoint-guarded batch is atomic, so an abort leaves no partial state); statements hard stop 175
proposals.PROPOSED_SOURCE_REQUEST_LIMIT: 3 per invocation (1 expected + the reader's 2 transient retries); 1 per canary unit when no retry occurs
proposals.PROPOSED_OBSERVATION_LIMIT: 27 expected, hard cap 30 (maxObservationsPerBatch = 30 so the unit is one batch of 109 statements, ≤ 120)
proposals.PROPOSED_OPERATOR_INVOCATION_LIMIT: 3 total (initial ingestion, a replay/NO_CHANGE verification, one later poll); at most ONE invocation may write the initial unit; no scheduler
stop_rules: any platform limit error (subrequest/query count, CPU 1102, daily quota) → STOP, no retry, no second attempt in the same window
any non-transient reader error → STOP (fail closed)
run left RUNNING → recover only by reap/resume after lease expiry
